My Mother died here, it was unacceptable.
My experience with Bang Lamung Hospital was beyond devastating. My mother was admitted there in a critical condition, and despite our concerns, the doctors insisted on keeping her there, assuring us they had everything under control. They promised to transfer her to Chon Buri Hospital if her condition worsened. However, none of the staff spoke English, which created a constant barrier for us as her family, desperate for updates on her condition.

From the moment she was admitted, we felt a profound lack of communication and care. It was over three hours before we were even called from the waiting room to receive any word about her condition. Then, without any warning or opportunity to say goodbye, she was abruptly taken to a quarantine room. We were standing right next to her but were not given even a moment to properly say goodbye before they whisked her away. After that, we were unable to see her or even contact her. Phone calls were restricted, and we were allowed to call only once a day to speak with a nurse. No doctor ever came to speak to us about her condition, and we were not given a single piece of paper or documentation detailing her health or treatment plan.

My mother had complex health issues, including systemic sclerosis and lung fibrosis, which placed her at high risk. Despite this, her possible gastric paresis and critical condition were largely ignored. The hospital staff failed to recognize the severity of her situation or to communicate with us in a way that allowed us to make informed decisions. They did not take any action to transfer her to Chon Buri Hospital as they had promised, and tragically, she passed away there.

We were told that she died of pneumonia, but given her conditions, we feel that her care was grossly inadequate. The worst part was finding her lifeless in bed, her body twisted unnaturally, eyes open, with no doctor present to explain or offer any comfort or clarity about her sudden passing. The lack of dignity, compassion, and professionalism we experienced at Bang Lamung Hospital was shocking and deeply traumatic. In my view, their neglect and incompetence cost my mother her life. I would not wish this experience on anyone and caution others about trusting this hospital with the care of their loved ones.

The procedure is as follows
You go to a self BP & oxygen testing machine.

You test yourself and take the test results to triage, the nurse initially ask for your symptoms and give you a sheet with details of which department to go and a token no for registration.

You go to registration counter and wait for your token to be called,make sure to bring passport and write your current address and phone no on a piece of paper.

The registration counter gives you a registration card and a paper with QR CODE.

You need to take this into the OPD department and give it to the nurse.

The nurse takes the paper and call you name when your turn comes.

Depending on your diagnoses you need to blood test and other stuff.
